transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-07-28
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Patel (Redwood SE), Sofia Ramirez (Head of AI - Evergreen), Daniel Park (Infra Lead - Evergreen), Aisha Khan (PM - Evergreen)

Summary (auto):
- POC goals: validate latency and cost for conversational search and recommender workloads; define success criteria and sizing for 4-week pilot.
- Decision criteria: latency p95, throughput needs, data residency/PII controls, TCO for expected qps, SLA needs.
- Next steps: send security docs, run benchmarks, share pricing, schedule follow-up.

Transcript:
00:00 - Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining - I'm Maya from Redwood. Quick roll call?
00:07 - Sofia Ramirez: Hi Maya, Sofia here. Daniel and Aisha on as well.
00:11 - Daniel Park: Yep hi.
00:15 - Liam Patel: Liam from Redwood, I'll be handling the performance side.
00:20 - Aisha Khan: Aisha. thanks.
00:28 - Maya Chen: Great. Agenda - confirm POC scope, success criteria, the workloads you want us to benchmark, and timeline. Is that right?
00:36 - Sofia Ramirez: Yeah that's perfect. We're trying to decide hosted vs dedicated vs private for our new conversational storefront, and we need numbers. Main constraints: latency p95 under 200ms ideally, but we'll discuss tradeoffs, and strict data residency / PII rules for purchase history.
00:57 - Liam Patel: Good - will note that 200ms p95 is aggressive depending on sequence length and model size. For reference, our hosted API with medium models typically hits 120-200ms p95 for short prompts, but with longer contexts and KB lookups it climbs.
01:18 - Sofia Ramirez: When you say medium models, which families?
01:22 - Liam Patel: We're talking 7B-13B-ish open models in our catalog, sometimes quantized. For higher quality we'd look at 33B+ which affects latency and cost. Also dedicated pools change the unit economics.
01:36 - Daniel Park: On Dedicated vs Private - our security team leans to Private if we can't get clear KMS integration and audit logs. Can you confirm what you support?
01:45 - Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM integrations, full audit logs, and can be deployed VPC or on-prem in restricted cases. We can share the security whitepaper.
01:55 - Aisha Khan: Great. For the POC, we want to run two workloads: conversational search (avg seq 120 tokens, peak 30 qps) and personalized recommendations (batch embedding generation, 500 reqs/min).
02:07 - Liam Patel: Ok noted. For conversational search, we'll size for 30 qps with 120-token sequences; that influences GPU choice and batching. For embeddings, that's mostly throughput - we can parallelize embedding workers.
02:22 - Maya Chen: For success criteria, can we confirm: 1) conversational p95 < 200ms, 2) embeddings throughput >= 500/min with an SLA on error rate < 1%, 3) security compliance with KMS and audit logs?
02:36 - Sofia Ramirez: Yes that's our starting point. Also we need cost per 1M tokens estimate for the POC to compare to our current provider.
02:44 - Maya Chen: We'll provide cost estimates for Hosted vs Dedicated (committed capacity) vs Private (license + infra ops).
02:51 - Daniel Park: Timeline - 4 weeks for initial POC, plus another 4-8 for pilot if results look good. Can you support that?
02:58 - Liam Patel: Yes, a 4-week POC is feasible: week 0 setup, week 1 small benchmark, week 2 longer soak, week 3 run regression & edge cases, week 4 wrap and results. We prefer a 3-day focused benchmark window mid-POC for apples-to-apples.
03:13 - Aisha Khan: What about data retention and deletion? We have to ensure no user PII is stored in hosted logs beyond X days.
03:20 - Maya Chen: Redwood Hosted can be configured with strict retention policies and encryption at rest; for absolute control, Private is the option since data never leaves your VPC.
03:28 - Sofia Ramirez: Understood. Can you run numbers for cost - I want TCO for 6 months under projected qps of 15 sustained, 30 peak.
03:36 - Liam Patel: We'll do that. We'll produce a cost model showing tokens, cost per 1M tokens, reserved instance discounts for Dedicated, plus ops cost estimate for Private.
03:45 - Daniel Park: On benchmarking methodology: we'll want synthetic and replay tests. Replay from our anonymized logs to measure cold vs warm cache.
03:52 - Liam Patel: Agreed - replay is key to evaluate caching/KV effectiveness. We'll ask you to provide two weeks of anonymized logs and a sample dataset.
04:03 - Sofia Ramirez: We'll prepare that. Also, what kind of telemetry will we get during the POC?
04:08 - Maya Chen: Full observability via Redwood Console: token-level latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards, tracing hooks and error rates. We can also provide raw metrics export to your datadog/splunk.
04:20 - Aisha Khan: Are there any gotchas when switching from Hosted to Dedicated? For example, model parity or fallback?
04:26 - Liam Patel: Not really, same model catalog, but Dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolated GPU pools. Fallbacks are supported - requests can be automatically routed to Hosted fallback if Dedicated capacity is saturated, subject to contract.
04:40 - Sofia Ramirez: What about quantization and model variants - would we be running int8 or other quantized models during the POC?
04:46 - Liam Patel: By default we'll test the production-quality variants we recommend; for cost experiments we can enable quantized kernels. We'll document quality delta and regen tests.
04:55 - Maya Chen: Okay let's walk through the POC proposal - I'll summarize: Redwood sets up a dedicated pilot (optional Hosted-only trial) and SE runs two benchmark suites: conversational search and embeddings. Success criteria as we discussed. Deliverables: benchmark report, cost model, security docs. Timeline: 4 weeks with benchmark window.
05:10 - Sofia Ramirez: Sounds good. A couple of detailed Qs: 1) how do you measure p95 - end-to-end including network to Redwood and back? 2) can we pin models and versions during the POC?
05:21 - Liam Patel: p95 will be end-to-end from our load generator to response completion. We'll also break down server-side p95 vs network. And yes, you can pin model versions - we recommend pinning for test reproducibility.
05:32 - Daniel Park: For Private deployment, what's the expected ops involvement from our infra team?
05:38 - Maya Chen: For Private we provide an installer and operator documentation; ops involvement varies. On VPC-deployed Private, we handle the control plane and you manage the infra config (subnets, peering, KMS). For fully on-prem, there's more engagement and a short professional services add-on.
05:55 - Aisha Khan: Any limitations on our side for embeddings throughput? We need burst capacity for black friday - can you autoscale?
06:02 - Liam Patel: Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling and burst capacity within committed pool constraints. For Hosted, autoscaling is handled by Redwood with usage-based billing. For Private, autoscaling depends on your infra and config; we can recommend patterns.
06:15 - Sofia Ramirez: Let's talk benchmarks specifics - can you run these setups: 1) Hosted (baseline), 2) Dedicated reserved pool, 3) Private (VPC) with same model and request profile?
06:25 - Liam Patel: Yes; note that Private raw latency may be better or worse depending on your network topology. We'll include network variance in the report.
06:33 - Maya Chen: We'll also run an ablation on KV cache: cold vs warmed prefix cache. That often explains big cost/latency differences.
06:40 - Daniel Park: For encryption at rest and in transit, we need AES256 and KMS integration with our HSM provider - is that supported?
06:48 - Maya Chen: We support KMS integrations; for HSM-backed keys we'll need to capture the specific provider details but generally supported in Private. Hosted can integrate with customer-managed keys in some enterprise plans.
06:58 - Sofia Ramirez: Great. Any legal/contract timeline issues we should be aware of? Procurement usually takes 2-3 weeks once we have an SOW.
07:05 - Maya Chen: That's typical. We'll try to get SOW & pilot contract drafted quickly after this call.
07:12 - Aisha Khan: One more - are there any model regression / quality monitoring features? We want alerts if generation quality drifts.
07:18 - Liam Patel: Yes, Redwood Optimize can run evals against prompt sets, alert on regressions, and tie to rollouts. We'll include a short demo in the follow-up if helpful.
07:30 - Maya Chen: Ok wrapping up - action items recap...
07:33 - Liam Patel: (mutter) sorry just a note about the KV cache test we should enable prefix caching for the conversational workload.
07:40 - Maya Chen: Recap: Redwood to share security docs and SOC2, SE to run benchmarks, AE to send pricing & SOW, Evergreen to share logs & dataset. Tentative benchmark window mid-POC.
07:54 - Sofia Ramirez: Agreed. Thanks all.
07:58 - Daniel Park: Thanks.
08:00 - Aisha Khan: Thanks.
08:03 - Maya Chen: We'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark kickoff and the next sync. Bye.

[transcription notes: occasional mis-heard words, speaker labels may be imperfect. Some timestamps approximate - main content aligns to 52-minute meeting length and includes planning & technical scoping details as recorded above.]
